post.caption:
Zero had to be invented twice. First as a placeholder marking an empty column, which is what makes positional notation and paper arithmetic possible at all. Try multiplying MDCCLXXVI by XLII and the problem becomes obvious immediately. Then as a number you can operate on, which Brahmagupta set out rules for in seventh-century India. It reached Europe through the Arab world, where several cities banned it as suspicious.
